Independent tests in simulated data

Source: R/simulate.R
independence.Rd

independence() is the assumption, used when simulating data, that the test results are independent given the disease status: among the diseased, and separately among the healthy, the result of one test carries no information on the results of the others. The function has no arguments. The object is passed to simulate_study() as its dependence argument, where it is the default.

Usage

independence()

Value

An object of class independence.

Details

Let \(t = (t_1, \dots, t_K)\) be a response profile, with \(t_k = 1\) for a positive result, and let \(Se_k\) and \(Sp_k\) be the sensitivity and specificity of test \(k\). The probabilities of the profiles among the diseased and among the healthy are the products $$P(T = t \mid D = 1) = \prod_{k=1}^{K} Se_k^{t_k} (1 - Se_k)^{1 - t_k}, \qquad P(T = t \mid D = 0) = \prod_{k=1}^{K} (1 - Sp_k)^{t_k} Sp_k^{1 - t_k}.$$

See also

simulate_study(), latent_dependence(), probit_dependence()

Examples

independence()
#> <independence> tests independent given the disease status
d <- simulate_study(n = 100, prevalence = 0.2, sensitivity = c(0.9, 0.8),
                    specificity = c(0.9, 0.95), verification_prob = 1,
                    dependence = independence())
